findings.checklist_item: Require the eventual bug close to carry `--caused-by=<origin-id>` even when the `caused_by` link was already recorded via `rebar link` at Phase 1 exit (or otherwise document how the close-time blame fallback is suppressed), so the authoritative attribution is not shadowed by a competing blame-derived edge.
evidence: transition_close.py:198-201 — `else: from rebar.metrics import blame; culprit = blame.derive_caused_by(...)` runs whenever `caused_by` is empty, with no check for an existing caused_by link on the ticket
Plan step 3 offers `rebar link ... caused_by` at Phase 1 exit as an alternative to `--caused-by` on close, but a close still occurs later and (absent --caused-by) will auto-derive
Problem statement's stated goal: replace the blame fallback that 'reliably charges the defect to the consumer's old ticket'
findings.finding: The `rebar link <bug> <origin> caused_by`-at-Phase-1-exit path (Plan step 3) does not suppress the close-time blame fallback: `_apply_caused_by` runs `blame.derive_caused_by` unconditionally whenever `--caused-by` is empty and never checks for a pre-existing `caused_by` link, so a subsequent close without `--caused-by` draws a second, blame-guessed edge beside the authoritative one — reintroducing the exact fallback the plan exists to displace.
findings.location: Plan step 3 ('rebar link <bug> <origin> caused_by when the link is wanted at the Phase 1 exit'); verified against src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:186-207 (_apply_caused_by)
scenarios: Agent records the authoritative origin via `rebar link` at Phase 1 exit, then in Phase 2 closes the bug with `--class` but no `--caused-by` (believing the link is already set) — blame auto-derivation writes a competing caused_by edge
findings.suggested_fix: In step 3 / the Reporting-back gate, state that whichever recording path is used at Phase 1 exit, the bug close MUST still pass `--caused-by=<origin-id>` (or `--caused-by` with the unattributable sentinel handling) — because a close without it re-runs blame auto-derivation and can add a competing edge.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion (grep or read-confirm) that verifies the attribution scoping to `defect`/`incomplete-implementation` and the Stage 1 git-history bullet pointer / fast-path retention note from step 7.
evidence: Step 5: 'Scope attribution to the `defect` and `incomplete-implementation` paths'
Step 7: 'note attribution retention on the fast path; point Stage 1's git-history bullet at the exit-gate step'
The 8 ACs cover steps 1,2,3,4,6, the carve-out from 7, plus frontmatter/diff gates — but not the scoping in step 5 nor the fast-path/Stage-1-pointer edits in step 7
findings.finding: Plan step 5 (scope attribution to the `defect` and `incomplete-implementation` paths) and two of step 7's sub-parts ("note attribution retention on the fast path" and "point Stage 1's git-history bullet at the exit-gate step") are described deliverables with no covering acceptance criterion.
findings.location: Plan steps 5 and 7; Acceptance Criteria list
scenarios: An executor could omit the scoping clause or the Stage 1 git-history pointer and still pass every listed grep, leaving described work unverified
findings.suggested_fix: Add e.g. `grep -n 'defect' ... ` anchored on the scoping sentence and a read-confirm bullet for the Stage 1 git-history pointer, so steps 5 and 7's remaining edits each map to a criterion.
